summary: The note describes the 2017 ICC Champions Trophy final, in which Pakistan comfortably beat India by 180 runs, the largest margin of victory in an ICC ODI tournament final. Pakistan, the lowest-ranked team entering the competition, won their first Champions Trophy and their first ICC ODI tournament title since 1992. The note also covers the individual awards and the head-to-head history between the two teams before the final, including India's 124-run win in the group stage on 4 June 2017.
one_line: Pakistan beat India by 180 runs to win the 2017 ICC Champions Trophy final, their first Champions Trophy title.
key_facts: Pakistan beat India by 180 runs in the 2017 ICC Champions Trophy final.
The 180-run margin was the largest margin of victory in the final of an ICC ODI tournament.
Pakistan became the seventh nation to win the Champions Trophy.
Pakistan's 2017 win was their first ICC ODI tournament title since 1992.
Pakistan entered the tournament as the lowest-ranked team in the competition and were massive underdogs.
Fakhar Zaman of Pakistan received the Man of the Match award for scoring a sublime 114 in the final.
Shikhar Dhawan of India received the Golden Bat award for scoring 338 runs in the tournament.
Hasan Ali of Pakistan received the Golden Ball award for taking 13 wickets in the tournament.
Hasan Ali was also adjudged the Man of the Series.
Prior to the final, India and Pakistan had met four times in the Champions Trophy, with each side winning two matches.
Pakistan's last win over India before the final was in 2009.
Since 2009, India had won seven consecutive games against Pakistan across ICC tournaments.
The most recent meeting was on 4 June 2017 in the group stages, where India won by 124 runs (D/L method).
Pre-match analysis expected a strong contest between India's batting lineup and Pakistan's bowling side.
